name: North and Western Lancashire Chamber of Commerce
what: The lead Employer Representative Body for the Lancashire LSIP, working with employers across North and West Lancashire.
why_contact: This is the organisation that wrote the LSIP by asking hundreds of local employers what skills they need.

name: East Lancashire Chamber of Commerce
what: Co-leads the Lancashire LSIP with the North and Western Chamber, representing employers in East Lancashire.
why_contact: They help make sure employer voices from East Lancashire towns feed into the plan.

name: Lancashire Combined County Authority
what: The strategic authority for Lancashire, Blackburn with Darwen and Blackpool, responsible for the Lancashire Growth Plan and devolved skills funding.
why_contact: They decide how a lot of adult skills funding is spent locally, based on what the LSIP says employers need.

name: Boost Business Lancashire
what: Lancashire's Growth Hub, offering free business support and advice to companies across the county.
why_contact: If you want to see how local businesses get help to grow, this is where they turn.

name: Lancashire Careers Hub
what: The local Careers Hub, funded by the Careers & Enterprise Company and delivered by Inspira, linking schools and colleges with employers.
why_contact: They run careers events, work experience and employer talks in Lancashire schools and colleges.

name: Lancashire Skills and Employment Hub
what: The strategic team, part of the Combined County Authority, that supplies labour market data and coordinates skills priorities across Lancashire.
why_contact: They publish the data behind this plan, including job vacancies and future skills needs.

name: Lancaster University
what: A top-ranked university based in Lancaster, offering degrees across engineering, science, business and more.
why_contact: A strong option if you want a traditional university course close to home.

name: University of Lancashire
what: Formerly UCLan, based in Preston with campuses across the county, offering a wide range of degrees and higher and degree apprenticeships.
why_contact: They work directly with local employers on courses linked to Lancashire's priority sectors.

name: Edge Hill University
what: A university based in Ormskirk, on Lancashire's southern edge, known for teacher training, health and creative courses.
why_contact: Worth a look if you're interested in courses in health, education or the creative industries.

name: Preston College
what: A large FE college in Preston offering A levels, technical courses and apprenticeships across many sectors.
why_contact: A good place to check for T Levels and apprenticeships linked to Lancashire's priority industries.

name: Blackpool and The Fylde College
what: An FE college named as one of the UK's Defence Technical Excellence Colleges, with strong links to aerospace, engineering and the visitor economy.
why_contact: If defence, engineering or hospitality interest you, this college has direct routes in.

name: Nelson and Colne College (East Lancashire Learning Group)
what: An FE college in Nelson, part of the East Lancashire Learning Group, offering A levels, technical courses and adult learning.
why_contact: A good option for A levels and technical courses if you're based in East Lancashire.
